newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Pope to visit Bosnian capital in April.
newsitem.headline: Pope to visit Bosnian capital in April.

text.p: Pope John Paul plans to visit the Bosnian capital Sarajevo in April at the invitation of the country's collective presidency, a representative for Bosnia's Roman Catholic cardinal said on Wednesday.
"The Pope will be coming to Sarajevo and it was agreed that it will be sometime in April," Ivo Tomasevic, secretary to Cardinal Vinko Puljic, told Reuters.
During the Bosnian war, the Pope was forced to cancel a scheduled visit to Sarajevo in September 1994. Separatist Serb forces laying siege to the city had warned they could not guarantee his safety.
"The Pope's programme will be similar to this unaccomplished visit from September 8, 1994," Tomasevic said.

During his trip, Pope John Paul will meet local Roman Catholic clergy, Bosnian government leaders and celebrate mass, he said. It was possible the Pope might choose to stay overnight in the city, Tomasevic added.
The Pope has spoken often of the four-year Yugoslav conflict and Sarajevo's siege, describing the city as a symbol of human suffering.
The three-man collective presidency, comprised of Moslem, Croat and Serb members, issued an invitation to the Pope in November to come to Sarajevo.

Alija Izetbegovic, a Moslem who led Bosnia's war-time government and is now chairman of the peacetime presidency, had always supported a papal visit as a way of reinforcing the country's multi-cultural tradition.
Orthodox Serbs accused the Vatican of favouring Catholic Croats during the war. But a year after the end of the Bosnian conflict, the Serb member of the presidency lent his support to the invitation.
The Pope visited neighbouring Croatia in 1994, drawing huge crowds in the capital Zagreb. He travelled to Slovenia, another former Yugoslav republic, last year.
